scope: private retained-descriptor VFS within existing journal crate; no new crate/dependency
main database uses admitted descriptor; WAL/rollback use retained native parent and file identities; C FILE_POINTER verifies actual owned object
Linux OFD locks implement SQLite byte protocol without builtin private inode state or global system-call replacement
one non-default process-lifetime driver, maximum 64 active namespace contexts including retired foreign file objects
DB/WAL/rollback/legacy SHM length ledger at callback growth boundary; existing wire/schema/cursor unchanged

sources.used: FILE_POINTER returns actual file object, not a public Unix FD; do not cast builtin private Unix layout or use optional FILESTAT diagnostics
driver must outlive connections; retained foreign files require process-lifetime registry and owned contexts
short-read zero fill and version-one methods contract
EXCLUSIVE before WAL permits no-SHM version-one VFS; process abort recovery is not power loss
OFD locks conflict with POSIX locks including same process, survive closure of other descriptions, and require l_pid=0
pinned SQLite DEFAULT_SECTOR_SIZE=4096, pending/reserved/shared byte protocol, exclusive WAL support; builtin name resolution is not descriptor authority

semantics.authority: ephemeral numeric namespace token is not a host pathname. Production Storage reuses cache native no-follow/private/ordinary/single-link/mount checks. Retained FD data I/O never reopens main name. Default VFS unchanged; only builtin clock/random/sleep delegated
semantics.sidecars: only WAL and rollback opened/deleted under retained parent. Legacy SHM accounted without open/delete. Unknown/temp/ATTACH/shared-memory/URI/exclusive-existing requests fail closed. Sidecar slots retain evidence after close; mismatch refuses reopening/deletion
semantics.lifetime: driver allocated once for process. Owner retirement removes token and fails subsequent file I/O, not already cached SQLite values. Foreign State owns Arc context and quota until close; new owner cannot revive old key. SQLite inherited connections must not be used after fork

limits.note: admission/transfer limits, not allocator/RSS, physical allocation, all operation state, or external-writer quota. Explicit NotFound alone represents missing optional files

semantics.locking: Linux F_OFD_SETLK/F_OFD_GETLK, zero PID; no unsupported-kernel fallback. Shared/reserved/pending/exclusive retry and downgrade follow SQLite byte protocol. Non-Linux Unix POSIX branch is test-only
semantics.unsafe: owned Slot/State layout and markers; catches Rust panic at C callback boundary. Valid pointers/serialized file methods are SQLite ABI requirements; no arbitrary pointer safety or OOM containment claim
semantics.durability: native file/retained parent flush requests; no atomic-write/safe-append/powersafe-overwrite device flags. 4096 sector hint is pinned SQLite default, not hardware measurement. Final check-to-relative-unlink race and post-operation flush uncertainty remain
semantics.tests: ordinary controlled Unix fixture Storage is independent of production native root. Actual bundled SQLite/default-VFS read/integrity and fresh-process locking/recovery oracles run on macOS; do not qualify Linux native mount/OFD/provider
semantics.resources: lean build retained; no new end-to-end timing/RSS claims, user payload deletion or Trash emptying

initialFailures.reason: macOS F_RDLCK/F_WRLCK/F_UNLCK are i16; Linux variants are i32. Accept Into<c_int> then convert to flock short field; preserve platform gating
manual NUL string literals rejected; replace with Rust C-string literals, no lint suppression

designCorrections: per-owner registered VFS drop could free a driver still referenced by an independently opened connection. Replace with one static driver and bounded owned registry contexts; regression covers actual foreign file lifetime and revoked I/O
retired owner alone must not release context quota while a foreign file still pins descriptors; isolated child confirms rejection at 64 and admission only after close
